questions.stem: Six angles measure $90^\circ$, $238^\circ$, $91^\circ$, $180^\circ$, $24^\circ$ and $205^\circ$. How many of these six angles are obtuse angles?

canonical_solution.text_md: An obtuse angle is bigger than $90^\circ$ and smaller than $180^\circ$. An angle of exactly $90^\circ$ is a right angle and one of exactly $180^\circ$ is a straight angle, so neither of those is obtuse.
Put the angles in order of size: $24^\circ$, $90^\circ$, $91^\circ$, $180^\circ$, $205^\circ$, $238^\circ$.

Compare each angle with the limits $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$. Acute (smaller than $90^\circ$): 1; right (exactly $90^\circ$): 1; obtuse (between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$): 1; straight (exactly $180^\circ$): 1; reflex (bigger than $180^\circ$): 2.
So 1 of the six angles are obtuse.

questions.stem: $AB \parallel CD$, with both lines drawn horizontally and $AB$ above $CD$. The points $S$, $P$, $Q$ and $T$ lie in this order on one straight line (the transversal) that crosses $AB$ at $P$ and $CD$ at $Q$, so $S$ is above $AB$ and $T$ is below $CD$. The points $A$ and $C$ lie on the left-hand side of the transversal, and $B$ and $D$ on its right-hand side. It is given that $A\hat{P}S = (2x + 21)^\circ$ and $D\hat{Q}T = (4x - 13)^\circ$. Calculate the size of $A\hat{P}Q$, in degrees.

canonical_solution.text_md: $A\hat{P}S = B\hat{P}Q$ (vertically opposite angles).
$B\hat{P}Q = C\hat{Q}P$ (alternate angles; $AB \parallel CD$).
$C\hat{Q}P = D\hat{Q}T$ (vertically opposite angles). Therefore $A\hat{P}S = D\hat{Q}T$.
So $2x + 21 = 4x - 13$, which gives $2x = 34$ and $x = \frac{34}{2} = 17$.
$A\hat{P}S = (2 \times 17 + 21)^\circ = 55^\circ$.
$A\hat{P}Q + A\hat{P}S = 180^\circ$ (angles on a straight line $SQ$), so $A\hat{P}Q = 180^\circ - 55^\circ = 125^\circ$.
